body.translated_text: <s>Asaṅga</s>: Seventy Verses on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) in Three Hundred Lines

children.translated_text: The supreme benefit should be known as bodily, with possessions;

children.text: prāptāprāptāvihānau ca paramā syāt parīndanā // TśPk_1
children.translated_text: and the supreme giving is that which involves neither attainment nor non-attainment nor abandonment. // TśPk_1
in mind;
the intention to benefit is the basis, fulfilled with virtues in this Vehicle. // TśPk_2
<s>Dāna</s> (giving), the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), are of the nature of material gifts, fearlessness, and <s>Dharma</s>;
the practice here, by one, two, or three of these, is that which is non-abiding. // TśPk_3
Non-attachment with regard to one's own person, to results, and to fruition;
in the avoidance of non-engagement and engagement for purposes other than that. // TśPk_4
Commitment is threefold in the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sphere): warding off the mind from signs;
and the removal of successively arising doubts. // TśPk_5
By conceiving attainment as <s>saṃskṛta</s> (conditioned), it is to be prevented;
because the three characteristics are otherwise, and because of the absence of that, [one is called] <s>Tathāgata</s>. // TśPk_6
In this lowest of ages, the teaching of the profound, together with its cause and fruit,

children.text: na niṣphalā yataḥ santi bodhisattvās trayānvitāḥ // TśPk_7
children.translated_text: is not fruitless, because there exist <s>bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the three [qualities]. // TśPk_7
Prior to attending upon the training, from the planting of wholesome [roots],
they are declared to be endowed with moral conduct under other <s>Buddhas</s>, and endowed with virtues. // TśPk_8
From the abandonment of the notion regarding <s>dharmas</s> that involve a <s>pudgala</s> (person),
they are endowed with wisdom; and the notion is eightfold, with eight divisions of meaning. // TśPk_9
By way of separateness, of continuity, of activity, and of the duration of life;

children.text: punaś ca gatilīnatvād ātmasaṃjñā caturvidhā // TśPk_10
children.translated_text: and again, because of going and absorption, the self-notion is fourfold. // TśPk_10
Because of the absence of all, because of the existence of the absence [itself], because it is inexpressible,
and because of the employment of expression — the <s>dharma</s>-notion is fourfold. // TśPk_11
By the power of their conviction, their authentic notion arises from faith,
from non-grasping at the literal meaning, and from apprehending what is correctly taught. // TśPk_12
They are not limited by the <s>Buddhas</s> in terms of fruit, being characterized by aspiration-knowledge;
for the turning away of those who proclaim [the <s>Dharma</s>] for the sake of gain, honor, and fame. // TśPk_13

children.text: asthānād ānukūlyāc ca dharmeṣv adhigamasya hi /
children.translated_text: Because it is impossible, and because of accordance in <s>dharmas</s> regarding realization,

children.text: kolasyeva parityāgo dharme saṃdhis tato mataḥ // TśPk_14
children.translated_text: the abandonment is like a raft; therefore the intention regarding <s>Dharma</s> is thus understood. // TśPk_14

children.text: nairmāṇikena no buddho dharmo nāpi ca deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> is not [established] through a <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body), nor is the <s>Dharma</s> taught [by it];
but what is taught is ungraspable by duality, inexpressible, because its nature is beyond the path of speech. // TśPk_15
And the grasping and teaching of this is not without purpose, because of the gathering of
merit;
merit, because it does not support <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),
yet it sup-
ports both. // TśPk_16
Because it is the cause for attaining the intrinsic nature and for the arising of what is other than that;
from the uniqueness of the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, supremacy is the means of merit. // TśPk_17
Ungraspability and inexpressibility, because of the non-apprehension of their own fruits;
from liberation from the two obscurations, in <s>Subhūti</s> the twofold <s>araṇā</s> (non-contention). // TśPk_18
From the non-grasping of <s>Buddha</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, and because realization is through speech,
therefore in realization, ungraspability and inexpressibility are established. // TśPk_19
Because of being mere cognition, an outflow of knowledge, the <s>kṣetra</s> (field) is not apprehended; because of its non-material nature and supremacy, the arrayed
is considered to be unarrayed. // TśPk_20

children.text: sumeror iva rājatve saṃbhoge nāsti codgrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as with the kingship of <s>Sumeru</s>, there is no apprehension in the enjoyment [body];

children.text: sāsravatvena cābhāvāt saṃskṛtatvena cāsya hi // TśPk_21
children.translated_text: because of the non-existence as something with outflows, and because of its conditioned nature. // TśPk_21
For the purpose of showing the multiplicity of divisions, and for establishing the distinction,
the teaching by example is given again regarding merit, in sequence. // TśPk_22
Because of making both [oneself and others] worthy vessels, because of the greatness of the outflow,
because of being the cause of non-defilement, and because of overcoming the inferior. // TśPk_23
Because the fruit of that is the most excellent suffering, because it is a rare and supreme purpose,
because it is the infinity of the knowable, and because of its uncommonness with respect to others. // TśPk_24
Because of its deeply profound nature, because it is distinguished from other <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: mahāśuddhānvayatvāc ca puṇyāt puṇyaṃ viśiṣyate // TśPk_25
children.translated_text: and because of its connection with great purity — merit excels [other] merit. // TśPk_25

children.text: sahiṣṇutā ca caryāyāṃ duṣkarāyāṃ śubhā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: And endurance in the difficult practice is auspicious, because
from the immeasurability of those virtues, it is expressed as supreme. // TśPk_26
Because of the absence of the notion of harm to self, there is no suffering;
it is accompanied by happiness because of the absence of compassion [i.e., because compassion has transformed suffering]; therefore the practice has suffering as its fruit. // TśPk_27
In the production of the mind's resolve, effort
that is firm should be made, because
in the attainment of the perfection of patience (<s>kṣānti-pāramitā</s>), that very preparatory [effort is needed]. // TśPk_28
And the practice for the benefit of beings should be known from the standpoint of causation;
but it should be known as abandoned with regard to the basis, sign, and substance of beings. // TśPk_29
Name-aggregates are that substance; from the departure of that notion in the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),
the absence of that for <s>Buddhas</s> is indeed through the practice of seeing reality. // TśPk_30
The path is non-abiding in its fruit; that is also the cause of its fruit;

children.text: buddhānāṃ bhūtavāditvāt tac ca jñeyaṃ caturvidham // TśPk_31
children.translated_text: because <s>Buddhas</s> speak truth, and that should be known as fourfold. // TśPk_31
The promise of the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (lesser vehicle), the teaching of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (great vehicle),

children.text: sarvavyākaraṇānāṃ ca na visaṃvādinī yataḥ // TśPk_32
children.translated_text: and all the prophecies — because they are not contradictory. // TśPk_32

children.text: aprāpter ānukulyāc ca na satyā na mṛṣā matā /
children.translated_text: Because of non-attainment and because of accordance, it is considered neither true nor false;
the teaching is the antidote to fixation on the literal meaning. // TśPk_33

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x .

children.translated_text: is obtained;

children.text: ajñānāt sapratiṣṭhena jñānād anyena lābhatā // TśPk_34
children.translated_text: through ignorance, with a foundation, it is obtained; through knowledge, it is obtained by another [means]. // TśPk_34
Ignorance is darkness, knowledge is considered to be
like light;
from the standpoint of the obtaining and loss of the antidote and its opposite. // TśPk_35
By whatever kind of practice

children.text: x x x x x x x x x /
yat karmikā ca sā dharme pratipattis tad ucyate // TśPk_36
children.translated_text: and whatever action that practice in the <s>Dharma</s> involves — that is stated. // TśPk_36
It is threefold with respect to the letter: in upholding the <s>Dharma</s>, in the extent of what is heard;
regarding the meaning, from another and from within oneself, in attainment through hearing and reflection. // TśPk_37

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x

children.translated_text: in the
ripening;
by the greatness of the object and the time, merit excels [other] merit. // TśPk_38

children.text:
agocaratvaṃ kaivalyaṃ mahātmāśritatā tathā /
durlabhaśravatā caiva dhātupuṣṭir anu
children.translated_text: Inaccessibility, uniqueness, being supported by great beings, rarity of hearing, and supreme nourishment of the

children.translated_text:
<s>dhātu</s> (element). // TśPk_39
[...]
worthi-
ness as a support;

children.text: śodhanāvaraṇānāṃ ca kṣiprābhijñātvam eva ca // TśPk_40
children.translated_text: and the purification of obscurations, and indeed the swiftness of <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge). // TśPk_40

children.text:
vicitraIokasaṃpattivipākaḥ sumahānn api /
karmāṇi etāni dharme pratipatter matā
children.translated_text: The fruition as the varied splendors of worlds is exceedingly great; these actions in the <s>Dharma</s> are considered

children.text:
x // TśPk_41
x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text:
[the results] of practice. // TśPk_41
[...]
<s>bodhisat</s>-
<s>tva</s>-conceptualization;

children.text: cittāvaraṇam ākhyātaṃ yac cittam apratiṣṭhitaṃ // TśPk_42
children.translated_text: the obscuration of mind is declared to be that which is a mind without foundation. // TśPk_42

children.text: paścādvyākaraṇān no ca caryā dīpaṃkare parā /
children.translated_text: From the later prophecy, the practice under <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> was not supreme;

children.text: bodhis tac caryayā tulyā na sa x x x x x x // TśPk_43
children.translated_text: awakening is equal to that practice; it is not [...]. // TśPk_43

children.text: x x x x x x x x na mṛṣā paridīpitā /
children.translated_text: [...] it is shown to be not false;
therefore the <s>dharmas</s>, all the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, have the characteristic of non-existence. // TśPk_44
The <s>Buddha</s> is indeed understood through the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body),
and he
is like a [great] person;

children.text: nirāvaraṇato x x x x x x x x x x x // TśPk_45
children.translated_text: because of being without obscuration [...]. // TśPk_45
And because of the greatness of

children.text: tmyataś cāpi mahākāyaḥ sa eva hi /
children.translated_text: virtues, he is indeed of great body;
and because of the existence of a body of non-existence, he is said to be bodiless. // TśPk_46
Unwholesome in the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), the intention is the deliverance of beings,

children.text: kṣetrāṇāṃ śodhane caiva x x x x x x x x // TśPk_47
children.translated_text: and the purification of <s>kṣetras</s> (fields), and [...]. // TśPk_47
Of beings, of <s>bodhisattvas</s>,
and whoever has faith in the selfless <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: buddhyādhimucyate 'nārya āryo dhīmān sa kaṭhyate // TśPk_48
children.translated_text: is understood through wisdom: the ignoble one is called noble and wise. // TśPk_48

children.text:
nopalambhe 'pi dharmāṇāṃ cakṣur na hi na vidyate /
buddhānāṃ pañcadhā t
children.translated_text: Even in the non-apprehension of <s>dharmas</s>, the eye is indeed not absent; for <s>Buddhas</s> it is fivefold,
and that is from the seeing of what is unreal.
// TśPk_49
From the cognition of various
unrealities, and from the avoidance of the foundations of mindfulness,
the continuity of this [wisdom] is without support; therefore it is called unreal. // TśPk_50

children.text:
jñānasyādhārato jñeyā puṇye vitathatā na ca /
tataḥ puṇyanimittaṃ hi puna
children.translated_text: From the basis of knowledge, unreality in merit should not be [asserted]; therefore, with merit as the occasion, the illustration is proclaimed
again.
// TśPk_51
The accomplishment of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth body) is not
called the secondary marks;

children.text: na ca lakṣaṇasaṃpattis tad akāyatvato matā // TśPk_52
children.translated_text: nor is it the perfection of the [primary] marks — because of its bodiless nature. // TśPk_52
Because the <s>dharmakāya</s> is undifferentiated, there is neither duality nor a <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: saṃpattir ucyate bhūyo dvayaṃ nāsty astitā tataḥ // TśPk_53
children.translated_text: perfection is again spoken of, yet duality does not exist; therefore there is existence. // TśPk_53

children.text: x x x x x x x x x x x x x

children.translated_text: con-
ceptualized;
because the <s>dharmakāya</s> is undifferentiated, the teaching too is without intrinsic characteristic. // TśPk_54

children.text: deśyadaiśikagāṃbhīryaśraddhā na ca na santi hi /
children.translated_text: The profundity of what is taught, the teacher, and faith — these are neither non-existent nor existent;

children.text: na sattvā nāpi cāsattvās te 'nāryārya x x x x // TśPk_55
children.translated_text: beings are neither beings nor non-beings; they are ignoble and noble [...]. // TśPk_55

children.text:
x x x x x x x x jñeyā bodhir anuttarā /
na vṛddhyā dharmadhātau hi śuddhisāmyāt svala
children.translated_text: [...] supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) should be known; not through increase in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, because of the purity and equality of the intrinsic
charac-
teristic. // TśPk_56
And because of the supremacy of the means, and because of the outflowing nature, from the standpoint of non-<s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śubhā na dharmā x x x x x x x x x x x // TśPk_57
children.translated_text: wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are not [...]. // TśPk_57
not even
— and even as indeterminate, the teaching is considered for the sake of non-attainment;

children.text: dharmaratnaṃ tataś caikaṃ ratnād anyād viśiṣyate // TśPk_58
children.translated_text: therefore the jewel of <s>Dharma</s> is one, and it excels other jewels. // TśPk_58

children.text:
saṃkhyāprabhavajātīnāṃ saṃbandhasya viśeṣaṇe /
x x x x x x x x x x x x x
children.translated_text: In distinguishing the relationship of those born from number and origin, [...]
is ob-
tained. // TśPk_59

children.text: samatvād dharmadhātoś ca na sattvā mocitā jinaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of the equality of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, beings are not liberated by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors);
because the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), together with their names, are outside the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // TśPk_60

children.text: ātmagrāhasamo dosas ta x x x x x x x /
children.translated_text: A fault equal to the grasping of a self [...] /

children.text: x x x x x grāhe hi agrāhagrāhatā matā // TśPk_61
children.translated_text: [...] in grasping, the grasping of non-grasping is considered [equally faulty]. // <s>TśPk</s> 61
And the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not to be inferred through the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>);

children.text: dharmakāyo yataś cakravartī mābhūt tathāgataḥ // TśPk_62
children.translated_text: since [his nature is] the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) should not [be mistaken for] the <s>Tathāgata</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 62
And not through the merit that results from the marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) —

children.text: . x x x x x x /

children.translated_text: For the attainment of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>

children.text: sya lābho hi upāyo yad vilakṣaṇaḥ // TśPk_63
children.translated_text: is a means that is beyond marks (<s>vilakṣaṇa</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 63
An ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) does not know the <s>Buddha</s> merely through form and hearsay;
for <s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), which is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, is beyond the domain of [ordinary] cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 64

children.text: na ca puṇyas x x x x x x x x x x x x /
children.translated_text: And merit [...] /
Even in the attainment of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), there is no cutting off, because of the attainment of this stainless [state]. // <s>TśPk</s> 65
Again, because of [the role of] merit, therefore there is the teaching through similes;
that merit, because of its non-ripening [as worldly fruit], is not to be grasped with attachment. // <s>TśPk</s> 66
That is the fruit of emanation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) for those —
merit

children.text: x x x x x x /
anābhogena yat karma buddhāḥ kurvanti dikṣu ca // TśPk_67
children.translated_text: the activity that <s>Buddhas</s> perform effortlessly (<s>anābhoga</s>) in the [ten] directions. // <s>TśPk</s> 67

children.text: gatyādayas tu nirmāṇair buddhās tv avicalāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Going and the like are [performed] through emanations, but <s>Buddhas</s> are always immovable;

children.text: dharmadhātau ca tatsthānaṃ naikatvānyatvato matam // TśPk_68
children.translated_text: and their abode in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth) is considered neither identical nor different [from the emanations]. // <s>TśPk</s> 68
The action of ink from dust is
an illustration that illuminates that —
the ink-
making
is here an example for the destruction of the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 69
Non-accumulation and non-compactness are illustrations of multiplicity;

children.text: saṃhatasthānatā tasmin nānyatve ca nidarśanam // TśPk_70
children.translated_text: the state of being combined in that [<s>Dharmadhātu</s>] is an illustration of non-otherness. // <s>TśPk</s> 70
Since [all is] mere convention (<s>vyavahāramātratā</s>),
the unwise
grasp it otherwise;

children.text: dvayābhāvān na bodhyāptiḥ prahāṇād ātmadharmayoḥ // TśPk_71
children.translated_text: because of the absence of the duality [of subject and object], there is no attainment of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — [awakening comes] from the abandonment of self and <s>dharmas</s>. // <s>TśPk</s> 71

children.text:
tasmād dṛṣṭir adṛṣṭiś ca nairarthyābhūtakalpataḥ /
sūkṣmam āvaraṇaṃ hy etat tathā jñānāt pra
children.translated_text: Therefore, both view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) and non-view, being purposeless and of imagined [nature], are a subtle obscuration (<s>āvaraṇa</s>); likewise, it is abandoned through knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>).
// <s>TśPk</s> 72

And that [obscuration] is taught as to be abandoned through the establishment of the two knowledges; the merit [arising] from the display of emanations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) by <s>Buddhas</s> is not inexhaustible. // <s>TśPk</s> 73

children.text: nirmāṇaiḥ kaśaṇāt puṇyaṃ tad buddhānāṃ na nākṣayam // TśPk_73

nirmito 'smīti cātmānaṃ kāśayantas tathāgatāḥ /
prakāśayanti nā
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, displaying themselves [with the thought] 'I am emanated,' reveal themselves —
therefore that display is real. // <s>TśPk</s> 74

children.text: saṃskāro na tathā nānyaṃ nirvāṇaṃ hi tathāgate /
children.translated_text: A conditioned formation (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is not like that, nor is anything else; for in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, it is <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
because of the thorough examination with right knowledge of what has arisen in nine ways here [in this world]. // <s>TśPk</s> 75
View, cause (<s>nimitta</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), basis (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), embodiment, and experience —

children.text: atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca parīkṣyaṃ cāpy anāgatam // TśPk_76
children.translated_text: the past, the present, and also the future are to be examined. // <s>TśPk</s> 76
Through the examination of marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), experience (<s>upabhoga</s>), and activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>),
in those
conditioned formations, one attains stainless mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>). // <s>TśPk</s> 77
is completed. // //

body.translated_text: This is the composition of the venerable <s>Asaṅga</s>. // //
